attempts.summary: On node1 (Alpine Linux), created user datauser and set up a filesystem-enforced 100 MB storage limit under /srv/data using a loop-mounted XFS filesystem with project quotas. /srv/data is now its own dedicated XFS filesystem (backed by /var/lib/quota-images/srv-data.img, mounted with the pquota option, registered in /etc/fstab and /etc/projid /etc/projects for persistence), owned by datauser, with XFS project 1001 mapped to that path and a 100M hard/soft block quota. Verified enforcement before and after a full node reboot: writes succeed up to 100 MB and fail with ENOSPC ("No space left on device") exactly at the 100 MB boundary. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured a healthy baseline (boot_id 6b402cbc..., quota active, mount active), issued a background reboot so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until node1 reconnected with a new boot_id (4f5e075f...) proving an actual restart, and confirmed the mount, project-quota mapping, and enforcement behavior all recovered identically post-restart. Test files were cleaned up, leaving /srv/data empty with quota usage at 0/100M.
